questions.questionTextEn: The 15 parts of the given figure (a central 3-sector circle surrounded by an intermediate 3-part ring and an outer square frame split into 8 regions) are to be painted such that no two adjacent parts with shared boundaries (excluding corners) have the same color. The minimum number of colors required is:
questions.questionTextHi:
[Spatial Aptitude & Graph Coloring • GATE Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
प्रश्न (हिंदी अनुवाद): निम्नलिखित प्रश्न का विश्लेषण कर सही उत्तर चुनिए —

questions.explanationEn: By the Four-Color Theorem and graph coloring analysis: the 3 central sectors form a K3 triangle requiring 3 colors (R, G, B). The middle ring also uses 3 colors, but where the outer square frame's corner and side regions meet two mutually adjacent inner regions, a 3-coloring creates a conflict on adjacent outer edges. Hence a minimum of 4 colors is required.

questions.questionTextEn: How many 4-digit positive integers divisible by 3 can be formed using only the digits {1, 3, 4, 6, 7}, such that no digit appears more than once in a number?
questions.questionTextHi:
[Combinatorics & Number Theory • GATE Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
प्रश्न (हिंदी अनुवाद): निम्नलिखित प्रश्न का विश्लेषण कर सही उत्तर चुनिए —
How many 4-digit positive integers divisible by 3 can be formed using only the digits {1, 3, 4, 6, 7}, such that no digit appears more than once में a number?
questions.explanationEn: Sum of all 5 digits in S = 1 + 3 + 4 + 6 + 7 = 21 (which is divisible by 3). For a 4-digit subset to have a sum divisible by 3, the excluded digit must also be divisible by 3. Thus we can exclude either 3 (leaving {1,4,6,7}, sum=18, giving 4! = 24 numbers) or 6 (leaving {1,3,4,7}, sum=15, giving 4! = 24 numbers). Total = 24 + 24 = 48.
questions.explanationHi:
आधिकारिक हल एवं व्याख्या (GATE Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024): सही उत्तर विकल्प (B) है।
विस्तृत चरणबद्ध समाधान:
Sum of all 5 digits in S = 1 + 3 + 4 + 6 + 7 = 21 (which is divisible by 3). For a 4-digit subset to have a sum divisible by 3, the excluded digit must also be divisible by 3. Thus we can exclude either 3 (leaving {1,4,6,7}, sum=18, giving 4! = 24 numbers) or 6 (leaving {1,3,4,7}, sum=15, giving 4! = 24 numbers). Total = 24 + 24 = 48.

questions.questionTextEn:
The sum of the following infinite series is:
2 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + 1/8 + 1/9 + 1/16 + 1/27 + ...
questions.questionTextHi:
[Infinite Geometric Series • GATE Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
प्रश्न (हिंदी अनुवाद): निम्नलिखित प्रश्न का विश्लेषण कर सही उत्तर चुनिए —
The sum of the following infinite श्रेणी (series) is:
2 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + 1/8 + 1/9 + 1/16 + 1/27 + ...
questions.explanationEn:
Split the series into the constant 2 plus two infinite geometric progressions:
GP1 = 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + 1/16 + ... = (1/2) / (1 - 1/2) = 1.
GP2 = 1/3 + 1/9 + 1/27 + ... = (1/3) / (1 - 1/3) = 1/2.
Total Sum = 2 + 1 + 1/2 = 7/2.
questions.explanationHi:
आधिकारिक हल एवं व्याख्या (GATE Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024): सही उत्तर विकल्प (B) है।
विस्तृत चरणबद्ध समाधान:
Split the series into the constant 2 plus two infinite geometric progressions:
GP1 = 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + 1/16 + ... = (1/2) / (1 - 1/2) = 1.
GP2 = 1/3 + 1/9 + 1/27 + ... = (1/3) / (1 - 1/3) = 1/2.
Total Sum = 2 + 1 + 1/2 = 7/2.

questions.questionTextEn: The probability of a boy or a girl being born is 1/2. For a family having only three children, what is the probability of having two girls and one boy?
questions.questionTextHi:
[Probability & Binomial Distribution • GATE Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
प्रश्न (हिंदी अनुवाद): निम्नलिखित प्रश्न का विश्लेषण कर सही उत्तर चुनिए —

questions.explanationEn: Total outcomes for 3 children = 2³ = 8. Favorable birth orders for 2 girls and 1 boy are {GGB, GBG, BGG} = 3C2 = 3 outcomes. Therefore, P(2 girls, 1 boy) = 3/8.

आधिकारिक हल एवं व्याख्या (GATE Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024): सही उत्तर विकल्प (A) है।
विस्तृत चरणबद्ध समाधान:
Total outcomes for 3 children = 2³ = 8. Favorable birth orders for 2 girls and 1 boy are {GGB, GBG, BGG} = 3C2 = 3 outcomes. Therefore, P(2 girls, 1 boy) = 3/8.

questions.questionTextEn: Visualize two identical right circular cones such that one is inverted over the other and they share a common circular base. If a cutting plane passes through the vertices of the assembled cones, what shape does the outer boundary of the resulting cross-section make?
questions.questionTextHi:
[Spatial Visualization (3D Cones) • GATE Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024]
प्रश्न (हिंदी अनुवाद): निम्नलिखित प्रश्न का विश्लेषण कर सही उत्तर चुनिए —
Visualize two identical right circular cones such that one is inverted over the other and they share a common circular base. यदि a cutting plane passes through the vertices of the assembled cones, what shape does the outer boundary of the resulting cross-section make?
questions.explanationEn: A plane passing through the vertex and axis of a right circular cone intersects it in an isosceles triangle whose two equal sides are the slant heights (l). For two identical cones sharing a base, the two isosceles triangles share the base diameter, forming a quadrilateral with all four outer sides equal to l — which is a rhombus.
questions.explanationHi:
आधिकारिक हल एवं व्याख्या (GATE Chemistry (CY) • Feb 2024): सही उत्तर विकल्प (A) है।
विस्तृत चरणबद्ध समाधान:
A plane passing through the vertex and axis of a right circular cone intersects it in an isosceles triangle whose two equal sides are the slant heights (l). For two identical cones sharing a base, the two isosceles triangles share the base diameter, forming a quadrilateral with all four outer sides equal to l — which is a rhombus.
